en: The *Xuetang Xing Heshang Shiyilu* (Record of the Omissions of Master Xuetang Xing) states that when Heshang Sishin resided at Cuoyan in Hongzhou, there was a shrine to King Qian’an behind his quarters; this was Li Sanjingyuan.
The local residents slaughtered animals for offerings without a single day passing. The Master detested this and moved the shrine to within the temple grounds.
To the west of that, he established a square hall upon the site. Not long after, while the Master was lying within it, a large python coiled its body beside him;

the Master rebuked it, and it fled. One night, he suddenly dreamed of a divine being wearing a tall cap who came before him and said, "Your disciple has been rebuked by you and can find no place of rest;
I wish to go to Guangnan. The Master granted his request in the dream, providing sixty attendants for the journey.
Before long, the number of deaths from the plague among the husband’s household reached the full count. Later, the Master asked his students, "Tell me, are there truly ghosts and spirits?
If you say there are, then why did I not kill Dead Heart? If you say there are none, then why did Zhuangfu die?
None of those who answered were in accord with the truth. Just then, the Head Seat from Zhenjing’s assembly arrived; the Master questioned him as before.
A questioner asked: "Yuan said, 'If the sweet melon reaches the stem, it is sweet; if the bitter gourd is connected to the root, it is bitter. The Master greatly rejoiced in this.
Yuan was a preeminent disciple of Biancai."
When Zen Master Zizai was among the assembly of the Fifth Patriarch, Yuanwu was serving as the Head Seat (Zaoyuan) for the ordination of monks.

The Patriarch ordered Zizai to go and investigate him. Reluctantly, Zizai went; when Yuanwu saw him coming, he said to him, "We have studied together; there is no need for you to come here to 'test the water' [probe my depth].
Zizai replied, "My own matter is not yet clear; I venture to hope for your compassion. Yuanwu said, "Do not deceive yourself, but..."

Wuzhuo said, "Prostrate! Prostrate! I can act as your teacher; you do not even understand the story he brought up. After [Deshan] himself had burned incense and performed his prostrations, Wuzhuo said, "Try bringing up the previous story again. Deshan said, "Deshan’s informal lecture does not answer questions. Wuzhuo then struck him. Deshan said, "I am an old man; why do you strike me? Wuzhuo said, "Because you are a fellow who speaks of the Way. Deshan said, "If you strike me once more, I will surely kill you. Wuzhuo said, "Strike first, then I will kill you. Deshan struck him, and Wuzhuo hit him back. As he was speaking, Wugu suddenly covered his mouth and said, "When it comes to this, simply look at it just like this.

He then went to the back of the hall, struck the ground with his sitting mat (*zuoju*), and said, "A pity! A pity! When the assembly asked him the reason for this, Wugu replied, "That case only instructs people to look at a single phrase.
Someone urged him, saying, "You must have firm faith; the Abbot must surely have a skillful means (*upāya*)."
Having encouraged himself as he was already a human being, he proceeded to investigate the matter. Within less than a month, he attained a realization (*kenshō*).
Later, he emerged from seclusion to reside at Wuzu Monastery. There, Yu Daopo of Jinling visited Master Langya Huiqi. Daopo made her living by selling oil-cakes.
One day, she heard a poor man singing a *Lotus Song*, which said: "Were it not for Liu Yi transmitting the letter, how could one have reached Mount Dongting?"

At Lake (Hú), she suddenly attained realization. She threw oil-cakes into the marketplace, whereupon her husband said, "You have gone mad. The old woman struck him with a palm and said, "This is not within your realm.
She then went to Langya to receive formal certification (*inka*). Thereafter, whenever she saw a monk, she would simply say, "Child."
As soon as the boy was about to deliberate, the woman shut the door. At that time, Xun Fodeng went to investigate her. Upon seeing him, she said, "Boy!
Boy! Xun said, "Mother! Mother! Where is my father? The woman turned around and bowed to a pillar.
Xun kicked it over and said, "I thought there was something truly extraordinary here. He then departed. The woman scrambled up and said, "Boy! Boy! Come back! I truly cherish you."

Xu simply did not look back. An Shouzuo also went to see her. The old woman asked, "Where have you come from? An replied, "From De Shan. The woman said, "De Shan Tai was my son. An asked, "Whose son are you, grandmother?

The woman said, "Upon being questioned by you, Senior Monk, I was so struck that I stood right there and urinated. The woman once composed a verse concerning Mazu’s "Not Being at Ease": The Great Way is not difficult; Just avoid picking and choosing. When love and hate are both absent, Everything is as it is. (Note:
The final line of the verse is often cited as "When love and hate are both absent, everything is as it is," though the specific phrasing here reflects the narrative context provided.)

The commentary states: "The face of the sun, the face of the moon, the empty sky, and lightning—though these may cut off the tongues of all the patch-robed monks under heaven, they clearly express only half of it."
As for Chan Master Jidao: he resided at Cuoyan (Emerald Cliff) in Hongzhou. When Zhang Wujin was serving as the Commissioner of Transport, he entered the mountains to visit him.
As Jidao came out to meet him at the gate, Wujin asked, "What is the environment of Cuoyan? He replied, "The gate is near the thousand-fathom well of Hongya;
the stone bridge divides the waters that wind around the pines and cypresses. Wujin took Jidao’s hand and said, "I have long heard of the name of the Way-master. Why..."
When he was able to respond with such reverence, Jixian said, "It is just so. Wujin laughed heartily and further recited:
"A wild monk welcomes guests down from the misty peaks; I ask you, what is the meaning of Cuiyan? The gate is near Hongya’s thousand-fathom well;
The stone bridge divides the waters as they wind through pines and cypresses. At that time, this was circulated among the community as a great event.
The Head Seat Huanglong Gong left the monastery to reside at Chanlin. He went to visit Master Farchang Yu, who asked him, "I have heard it said that you intend to burn incense for Huanglong;
is this true? Gong replied, "I dare not. Yu said, "A dragon gives birth to a dragon;
one must be able to raise clouds and spit mist before one can succeed. Gong said, "It depends on the resources available to the household. Yu said, "You have not yet lifted the incense."
"Long ago, I already set aside Huanglong. Cong said, "Do not be so talkative. Yu said, "Tell me, where is Huanglong’s true head?
Cong lifted up his sitting cloth (*kaṣāya*). Yu called for an attendant to bring him a sitting cloth;
as the attendant held it in his hand, Yu struck him and said, "Thirty years from now, you will still say that you have seen this old monk."
After [Fahui] passed away, Huigong resided at Huaguang Temple on Mount Heng, where he maintained a style of strict discipline. He was a man of humble means, wearing the robes of a commoner.
When Huaguang Temple was consumed by fire, Huigong’s *Yulu* (Recorded Sayings) remained within the ashes; the calligraphy was undamaged, while the rest of the paper was completely incinerated.
This is truly a manifest verification of the power of Prajñā. Huigong was a native of Shangrao; he received his formal training at Boshan and was a contemporary of Chan Master Daoyou.

His fellow practitioner, Chan Master Wen-shu Neng, possessed a naturally serene and leisurely disposition and was content with austere stillness. He once offered this verse on "Three Pounds of Hemp": "The samādhi before one's eyes;

calculating the water as it strikes the millstone. To leak out the celestial mechanism is to lose one's money and incur punishment. He also offered this verse on the "Fire in the Twelfth Month": [text missing].
Shao Shan said, "The birds know the wind; the crickets know the rain. How pitiable is Xie Sanlang, rowing his boat all alone under the moon.

When Yuanwu was residing at Daolin, he always held him in high esteem. Once, the Governor of Wuling, Zhang Tongzhi, sent a letter to Yuanwu stating that there were no venerable masters in Ding and Li with whom he could converse.
Yuanwu subsequently recommended Neng, noting that he was a preeminent disciple of Zhenjing.
Zao Jishen invited Yuanwu Keqin to his residence. Upon seeing that Keqin’s appearance was austere and his demeanor dry and simple, Jishen paid him no mind at all;

he merely performed a long bow and withdrew. Not long after, when Yuanwu had attained enlightenment, Jishen sent an edict ordering him to join the assembly of Tongzhi to discuss the five houses of Chan.
Yuanwu’s eloquence flowed like a rushing river, and only then did Tongzhi come to revere him, remarking to Yuanwu: [The text provided ends here.]
He said: "Had it not been for my teacher, I would have nearly lost a venerable elder.
Master Shun of Baiyang addressed the assembly while ill, saying: "During my long illness, I have never once pushed aside my wooden pillow. When people come, they mostly ask, 'How is it?
I, this mountain monk, answer according to the circumstances as they arise. Outside the window, the yellow oriole has even more to say. Among the assembly...
The Master said, "Let me try to point out the source of the illness for this mountain monk. In this seven-foot body, where does the illness reside?
The assembly offered various responses, but none were in accord. The Master then clapped his hands once on their behalf, opened his mouth, and made a sound like retching.
He further remarked, "What a fine wooden pillow!"
The Venerable Fohsing resided at Deshan during his time in the world. He dispatched the Head Seat An to Jiangshan to deliver a letter of succession.
Upon receiving the letter in the Dharma Hall, Yuanwu said, "It has traveled a thousand miles to reach you; you have not disgraced our ancestral tradition.
The public case is already established—how do you communicate it? An replied, "Presented face-to-face, there is no room for evasion. Yuanwu said, "This is from Deshan..."
At the foot of the mountain, [Wuzhuo] asked, "Which one is the Senior Seat’s? An said, "How could there be a second person?
Wuzhuo said, "What about the one behind you? An then passed the letter to him. Wuzhuo said, "A master Chan guest has naturally what it takes.
An said, "I entrust this to Jiangshan. Next, they went before the Sangha Hall. An held up the letter and greeted the Head Seat. The Head Seat said, "Xuansha’s white paper—this..."
"From where have you come? Ancheng took up the letter and said, "Do you see it? Zuo reached out his hand and received the letter.

Ancheng held the letter and said, "I have long kept this essential point in silence, not wishing to speak of it hastily. Today I present it to you; I hope you will deign to read it once. Zuo then gave a shout. Ancheng said:
The Head Seat, Jue, also shouted. An then struck him once with his staff.
As Jue hesitated, An said, "If you do not understand three, eight, or nine, you cannot help but brood. He struck again and said, "Receive!
Yuanwu and Fuyan saw this from the Dharma Hall. Yuanwu said, "My Head Seat has been killed. Fuyan said, "Official horses kicking each other. There was [laughter].
This was a very serious matter. When Huian heard of it, he remarked, "What are you talking about—'official horses kicking each other'? This is truly 'dragons and elephants treading upon one another.
Wuzhuo summoned him and asked, "I am the head seat among my assembly of five hundred; why did you strike him? Huian replied:
"The Master must also take a beating before he will understand. Wuzu looked at Foyan, who stuck out his tongue. Foyan said, "Not yet.
He then turned to An and asked, "Holding a hoe in empty hands, walking while riding a water buffalo; a person passes over the bridge, yet the bridge flows while the water does not.
What is the meaning of this? An bowed deeply and said, "All that I have submitted is entirely truthful. Foyan laughed heartily.
He laughed and said, "So you are truly one of the family. Huineng then went to the Fifth Patriarch, Master Zizhi, to deliver the letter.
Zizhi asked, "What does it say in the letter? Huineng replied, "The patterns are already manifest. Zizhi asked, "Ultimately, what does it say?
Huineng replied, "Brandishing a precious sword in broad daylight. Zizhi said, "Come closer. Here, we do not recognize a single character. Huineng replied, "Do not—"
Faking a retreat, Xizai looked at his attendant and said, "This is a monk from where?
An said, "Don't. The attendant replied, "This senior monk was once in the Master's assembly. Xizai said, "No wonder he is so slippery-headed.
An said, "He has indeed been treated with blunt indifference by the Master. Thereupon, Xizai took the letter and held it over the incense burner, saying: "Namo Samantabhadra..."
Dhānam. An simply stepped forward and snapped his fingers; the letter opened of its own accord. An returned to Mount Jiang to spend the summer retreat.
Yuanwu instructed him to ordain monks. When the summer retreat ended, Deshan sent someone to welcome An.
While An was preparing his travel gear, Yuanwu arrived and asked, "What do you require for your journey tomorrow? An replied, "I seek several dozen *zhang* of short song paper."
"A long discourse can be exhausted in just two or three words. Wusu then sent him off with this verse: "The envoy does not disgrace his mission;
in facing the moment, one prizes the ability to respond directly. To sit in meditation while stroking a tiger’s whiskers—every step transcends the mundane world.

Not only was he arranged beneath the bright window, but he was drawn before the Zen seat and pressed against the precipice. Grasping the mallet and raising the fly-whisk, he unleashed his heroic eloquence; its resonance was like the ringing of metal and the vibration of jade."

A rushing thunderclap! For ninety days he has held aloft the essential principles of the school; disciples gather in great numbers, long following his wind. His method of untying adhesions and removing fetters is sharp and biting;
even in driving the plow and seizing the food, he remains composed and dignified. Summer ends and he longs for the mountains to return;
having settled the affairs of Wuling, the profound depths of the Dharma-treasury reside within his breast. Walking on, he need not fear lacking those who understand him. As he departs—
Seeking a verse for my parting gift: a thorn from a *kṣīrikā* tree wrapped in a *vajra*-circle. A short song requires dozens of feet; a long stanza needs but three or two words.
The golden-maned lion knows how to turn its body; such is the one who stands as a preeminent figure in the monastic groves.
Before long, the solitary peak let out a great roar; with five leaves and one flower, heaven and earth were filled with spring.

Later, he established the Dharma at Lingyan and succeeded Fuxing Hui Chan Master. He was a native of Wuzhou and received the Dharma from Master Chen of Yuwang. He resided at Xiyuan in Nanjian. New [edition].
Hui was performing the ritual for delimiting the boundaries of a sacred precinct. He cleared away tea bushes and planted pine and cypress trees.

When people complained to the authorities, they pursued him with great severity. Hui said, "Wait a moment; I am on my way. He immediately shaved his head and bathed, then ascended the hall to take leave of the assembly, saying:
"The summons of official messengers does not cease for a moment; how can it compare to clearly understanding the affairs of the long past? Previously, there was a song of non-arising; now—"
Delighted that his spiritual cultivation had reached completion, he passed away with eyes closed. The authorities subsequently laid the matter to rest.
Chan Master Deng of Taiping in Shuzhou was well-versed in the sutras and treatises, yet he also taught the exposition of Chan. Master Baiyun Yan sent him a verse, which said:
"The moon atop Mount Baiyun, The shadow beneath the pines of Taiping. On this fine night, there is no wild wind."
It all becomes a single field of experience. Dengde recited this verse, and before long, he thoroughly penetrated the profound depths of the Chan school.
Later, Master Xuedang said: "Regarding the latter two lines, students often increase their intellectual pathways;
it would be better simply to look at the first two lines, for therein naturally lies the direct and correct principle for administering medicine to those who have fallen ill."
Chan Master Jingyin Cheng, together with the Dharma masters Zhen, Yuanwu, and Cishou, as well as ten great Dharma masters, held a vegetarian feast at the residence of Grand Marshal Chen Liangbi.
At that time, Emperor Huizong visited in private to observe the assembly. A master of the Avatamsaka Sutra questioned the Chan masters before the assembly, saying:
"In the teachings established by our Buddha, from the Small Vehicle up to the Perfect and Sudden, all conceptualizations are swept away."
Emptiness and existence must be realized as the solitary, true, and eternal; only then, adorned with the myriad virtues, can one be called a Buddha.

When a Chan master’s single shout transforms the ordinary into the sagely, it seems to contradict the various sutras and treatises. Now, if this single shout can penetrate the five teachings, [it is not contradictory].

"This is the correct teaching. If one cannot enter [this understanding], this is a false teaching. Master Cheng of Zhuchan contemplated this and said, "What the Dharma Master has asked is not sufficient for the response of these three great Chan masters.
The Junior Elder of Jingyin can cause the Dharma Master to be free from delusion.
Cheng summoned Master Shan; Shan responded with an assent. Cheng said, "The Dharma Master’s notion that the Buddha-dharma is small..."
The teaching of the Vehicle possesses meaning. The Initial Teaching of the Mahāyāna is the meaning of emptiness.
The Final Teaching of the Mahāyāna is the meaning of neither being nor non-being. The Sudden Teaching of the Mahāyāna is the meaning of being and emptiness simultaneously.
The Perfect Teaching of the One Vehicle is the principle that it is not empty yet not existent, and not existent yet not empty.
For example, my single shout is able to penetrate not only the five teachings, but even reaches into the hundred crafts and arts, as well as all the various schools of thought.
Cheng then gave a shout and asked Shan, "Did you hear it? Shan replied, "I heard it. Cheng said, "Since you..."
[Cheng] asked, "Did you hear it? Wen said, "I heard it. [Cheng] said, "Then this one shout exists; it can lead one into the Small Vehicle (Hīnayāna) teachings.

Cheng then called to Shan, saying, "Did you hear it? Shan said, "I did not hear it. Cheng said, "Since you did not hear it, then that previous shout was non-existent; it can lead one into the Initial Teaching (Ādikarmika).
Cheng again looked at Shan and said, "When I first gave the shout, you said there was one. Now that the sound has long since faded away, you..."
Furthermore, if the Way is non-existent, then the primordial beginning must truly exist; if the Way is existent, then it must truly be non-existent today.
By being neither existent nor non-existent, one can enter the Final Teaching. Cheng also said: "When I let out a shout, existence is not existence, for it exists because of non-existence.
When there is no shout, non-existence is not non-existence, for it is non-existent because of existence. Thus, existence and non-existence are simultaneous. This can...
Entering the Sudden Teaching, Cheng also said: "This one shout of mine does not function as a single shout;

it transcends existence and non-existence, and both intellectual understanding and conceptualization are forgotten. When the Way is present, not even a speck of dust is established; when the Way is absent, it extends horizontally throughout empty space.
Thus, this one shout enters into hundreds of thousands of myriads of kotis of shouts, and hundreds of thousands of myriads of kotis of shouts enter into this one shout. This is capable of...
Entering the Perfect Teaching (Yuanjiao), Shan did not realize he had risen from his seat. He prostrated himself before Cheng. Cheng spoke again to Shan, saying:

"It is not only in this single shout that it is so. Even in speech and silence, movement and stillness—at all times, in all places, regarding all things and all matters—it accords with principle and accords with capacity, pervading everything without exception. Thereupon, the fourfold assembly rejoiced upon hearing this.
Having never heard this before, His Majesty the Emperor was greatly pleased.
The Monk Furu, who had appeared in the world to reside at Mount Jing, was invited by the Prefectural Governor to open the hall at Lingyin Monastery. After descending from the seat, Feng...
The Vice Minister asked, "Master, you once said, 'I will not act like this little insect.
Why then did you fail? Foyue replied, "The entire earth is Upādhyāya Gaomo; how can you search for it? Feng hesitated, and Foyue struck him with his palm.
At that moment, the assembly turned pale with alarm, but Feng laughed heartily and said, "I have met the Buddha-dharma of the Elder face-to-face. Later, he reported this to Baiyang Shun.
Upon hearing this, the Abbot took Deheng’s place and raised his hand, saying, "I am mindful that you are becoming a new elder.
He then took Furitsu’s place and lifted up his *kāṣāya*, saying, "How many people desire it, yet are unable to obtain it?"
The head seat Yuanli studied at Jiaoshan. Initially, he visited Master Yan at Taiping in Shu;

whenever he entered the room for instruction, Yan would say to him, "Monks of our tradition must clearly distinguish between the black and the white. After two years, Yuanli suddenly realized his own insight.
They went to the Abbot’s quarters. Fayan nodded his approval. When Fayan was appointed as the Fifth Patriarch, they both went with him according to protocol.

At that time, Foyan was only seventeen years old and had also joined the master’s assembly. Whenever there was a question posed, Fayan would say, "I am not your equal; you understand this well yourself."

Someone said, "I do not understand; I am not as good as you. The Buddha-Eye (Foyan) was thus in doubt and unable to resolve it, so he asked, "Who among those in the assembly has mastered the Master’s way of speaking?
Yan replied, "I once told Senior Monk Li that one must possess the eye that distinguishes the black from the white to truly study the Way.
Li, however, understands it. Foyan then sought instruction from Li. After several years had passed, [Foyan attained realization].
He was just about to explain its meaning when Liangyan appeared. Liangyan was still in good health. A monk came from Longmen, and Liangyan asked him, "What sayings or phrases did you hear at Longmen?
The monk replied, "Someone asked, 'What does the golden-scaled fish that has passed through the net eat? and the answer was: [it eats]..."
"Lao-lung refuses to stay; though called, he does not turn his head. Li said, "Brother Yuan’s name is truly well-earned.

Xuedang once had a verse that said: "I do not understand, yet I am not as good as you. Bodhidharma has two missing teeth upon his gate. Throughout the hall, there is boundless wind among the white artemisia;
Clearly, it does not arise from the autumn river itself. He also said: "I do not understand, yet I am not as good as..."
How laughable! A thousand flowers bloom upon the tip of a pestle; Sudhana wanders in vain through a hundred cities. When has he ever trodden upon his own ground?
During the Chongning era, Xuedou Lili returned once more to the Third Patriarch’s site. A monk asked, "Where are you going?
Lili said, "Having eyes but no ears, sitting by the fire in the sixth month. The monk asked, "I do not understand the meaning of this. Lili said, "My home..."
Being poor is still tolerable; being poor on the road is what kills one with grief. Again, there was a question:
"The *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* says, 'All wholesome dharmas. What are wholesome dharmas? Ligqi said: "Above is heaven; below is earth; sitting in between is sitting."
Lidili asked, "What do you call 'wholesome dharmas'? Later, he paid his respects to Lao [Yuan] at Suiyan in Siming.
Wang Zhengyan (whose name was tabooed by the Emperor), serving as the Transport Commissioner for Jiangxi, had long studied under Huìtáng but did not reach accord.
One day, he asked, "Who is it that has attained the profound Dharma of the Master? Huìtáng replied, "There is an elder named Xinyún at Yúnyán. Wang went to visit Xinyún and questioned him.
Zhengyan said, "I have heard that birth occurs through the conjunction of three conditions, and I have also heard of 'dying and being born immediately.

Why is it that there are those who take over a womb (*tāi*) to be born? I truly have doubts about this. Xin said, "Suppose you, Zhengyan, were appointed as a Grand Canal Commissioner (*zào*). Wherever you went, you would immediately occupy that position.
Would you still have doubts? Zhengyan said, "I would not doubt it. Xin said, "If you do not doubt this, why do you doubt that? Zhengyan was speechless.
He attained realization upon hearing these words;
his realization was perfect and outstanding. After receiving the seal of certification from Tianyi Huai, Xiu traveled extensively, eventually arriving at Fushan.

As soon as Yuan saw him, he recognized his potential and intended to take him under his wing. He presented him with the Nine Banners (jiu dai), saying, "I have composed these Nine Banners, yet I have never shown them to anyone."
"Try to examine this for me. Xiu already understood the intention behind the request; he left a verse and then departed, saying: "If the root of the topknot is firmly grasped, then rest.
In a single day, who has leisure for two hair-combs? In essence, his physical frame is naturally fine; even without applying rouge and powder, he is elegant."
Chan Master Lingyuan Qing resided at Taiping. While passing through Wuzu’s monastery, he was asked to provide a judgment on the kōan concerning the "large radish of Zhenzhou.

After the master had finished his discourse, he said, "All of you have come directly from Zhenzhou," and then descended from the seat. Yan took Qing by the hand and said, "So, you are truly one of my own family.
Later, another elder arrived at Wuzu’s monastery; as he entered the gate— (Note: The provided text ends abruptly with "祖門," which translates to "Wuzu's gate" or "the gate of the patriarch.")
Upon his arrival, [Dongshan] immediately asked, "When Lingyun saw the peach blossoms, what did he do? The old master replied with a stern voice, "The story remains.
Yan laughed and led him back to the abbot’s quarters. Later, Qingchang said to his students, "In the Gate of the Patriarchs, a true person is difficult to find.
Since leaving Huaitang, the only true master I have encountered is my elder brother, Dongshan. Thus, he wrote this inquiry.

There was no month that passed without [the Master] paying his respects. When the Buddha (Fó) observed his departure from the Patriarch (Zǔ), the Patriarch asked, "Where are you going? He replied, "To Taiping. The Patriarch said, "Very well.
Subsequently, he succeeded to the seat.
Jiuxian Qing succeeded the Venerable Huiru Ya. He lived in seclusion at Mount Jing.
When Furi appointed Qing as the Head of the Assembly (Zaoyuan), Qing declined, saying, "The assembly of seventeen hundred people are all heroes and sages; how would I dare stand before them?
Furi insisted and would not allow him to refuse. Furi said, "It is just like the saying: 'If you raise one, you cannot raise two. To let one point pass is to fall into the third."
"Second, what do you think? Qing said, "The alert are alert; the dazed are dazed.
Ri said, "How could he not have become the Head Seat of Jingshan? Thereupon, he accompanied the assembly in seeing him back to his quarters.
Master Min of Mount Emei’s Central Peak first lectured on the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* in Chengdu. When Yuanwu resided at Zhaojue, Min frequently went to enter his room for instruction.
Yuanwu instructed him to compose a verse on the theme “The Pattern is Already Manifest” in all circumstances.

Once, while Yuanwu was expounding the *Ten Mysterious Gates* to the assembly, a monk raised the question: “When you ask about the seal of the mind, what does it look like? Yuanwu replied: “The pattern is already manifest.”

Chang suddenly attained a realization and sought formal certification (*inka*). Wuzhuo showed him the hammer and tongs of the fundamental division (*benfen*), leaving Chang with no opening for speech.
One day, Chang said to Wuzhuo, "Master, do not raise a koan; wait until I have spoken it out. Wuzhuo said, "Very well. Chang said:

"Ordinarily, when one raises the mallet or brandishes the whisk, is this not what the sutras teach—that all things existing in all worlds are none other than the wondrous, luminous true mind of bodhi?
Wuxu laughed and said, "So you have been making your living right here all along!"

Wu questioned him further. The man replied, "When I shouted 'Down! and struck the meditation seat, was that not 'returning the hearing to hear one's own nature,' whereby that nature achieves the Unsurpassed Way?
Wu asked again, "Have you not seen it stated in the sutras that the wondrous nature is perfectly luminous and free from all names and signs?
At these words, the man was suddenly enlightened. Wu departed from Shu and resided at Jia Shan; the man also ceased his lectures.
Upon his arrival, he attended the evening *zana* (private instruction). [Zhaozhou] raised a case: A monk asked Yantou, "How is it when the ancient sail has not yet been hoisted?
Yantou said, "The donkey in the back garden is eating grass. Min was utterly bewildered and did not know where this pointed; he reported this to Wuzhuo. Wuzhuo said, "Ask me yourself. Min then asked.
"Before the ancient sail was hoisted, what was it like? Huineng said, "The cypress tree in the courtyard. Thereupon, Wumen attained great enlightenment.
Not long after, Huineng appointed Wumen as the Head Seat (Zuoyuan). He composed a verse saying: "Do not boast of having finished the *Four-Part Vinaya* or the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*;

Press down the clouds and investigate thoroughly from the very depths. Do not emulate Master Daoliang who went personally to Mazu; It is better to be like Deqiao who visited Longtan. Seven years passed..."

He returned to Zhaojue; for three years he soared above the azure cliffs. Today, he is troubled by the request to serve as the First Seat (Diyizuo), appearing like an udumbara flower amidst a thicket of blossoms.
When Min first visited Wujin at Zhugong, they discussed the teachings of the Vehicle (Jiao-cheng). Wujin was greatly pleased.
Later, hearing that Min had been appointed as the First Seat, Wujin sent a letter to Wu saying: "Master Min has abandoned his principles."
Xue opened the eye of the school's founding principle, like a Persian ship laden with precious jewels that, meeting a favorable wind, reached the shore.
One day, Min said to Wu, "The ancients said, 'It is like a single drop cast into a vast ravine. Yet they did not realize it was actually the great ocean being cast into a single drop.
Does the Old Monk approve of these words? Wu replied, "Look at this; what can you do about it?"
One day, Baiyun Chuan raised this case in his room, citing Yunmen’s public address: "Yunmen showed the assembly such large chestnuts; how many could you possibly eat?
None of those present offered a response that accorded with the truth. He then asked Yan, who said, "Hanging up a goat's head while selling dog meat. Chuan was struck with awe by this.

Yan once said, "I have been practicing for twenty years, and only now do I recognize my shame. Later, when Lingyuan heard this, he sighed and remarked, "Those two characters, 'recognizing shame,' are excellent.

He then composed the *Zhengxu Ming* (Inscription on the Continuation of the Correct) and included it therein. A layman came to Yan seeking to leave the household life, saying, "I wish to abandon my worldly conditions (*sheyuan*).
Yan asked, "What do you mean by 'abandoning conditions'? The man replied, "To abandon one's wife and children—this is what I call abandoning conditions."
Yan said, "I too have a wife; do you believe me? The scholar remained silent. Yan then recited this verse:
"I have a wife, Whom no one in the world has seen. Day and night we dwell together, Spontaneously possessing skillful means."
The monk Chong resided at Touzi. He was over eighty years old. One night, the head monk (jian-si) was murdered by someone.

The deputy steward informed Chong, who said, "Do not alarm the assembly; I already know who the person is. When the deputy steward reported this to the authorities and the officials arrived, Chong spoke as he had before.
The official asked, "Where is the man? Chong replied, "It is I, the old monk. The official then compelled Chong to be imprisoned. At that time, Yang...

Next, Gongwei served as the Prefectural Governor. While traveling on inspection and entering the borders of the prefecture, he dreamed of a divine being who said, "In this prefecture, there is a Bodhisattva in human form who sits unjustly bound in iron shackles.
Yang immediately went to search for him. The officials informed Yang of the matter concerning Chong, whereupon Yang released him. Ten years later—
There was a practitioner who suffered from *kāmalā* disease and confessed, saying, "I am the one who killed the monastery supervisor.
Huang Daoshou once wrote in a letter to Hu Shaopi: "Your cultivation of the Way has yielded considerable results; this is the method for treating illness."
One should seek deeply the joy of dhyāna to illuminate and shatter the root of birth and death; then, anxiety, affliction, lust, and anger will have no place to set foot.
Once the disease has no root, its branches and leaves can do no harm. Touzi Conghai’s exposition was profound and his practice of the Way was lofty and revered.

Those who do not fall short of the ancients are all worthy of being approached. However, if one studies false speech and flowery rhetoric from scholars of mere literary style, this is to increase the seeds of ignorance.
Even in my old age, I especially delight in receiving wise gentlemen and officials; when we open our hearts to debate, I can immediately pierce through the nostrils of all the Confucian scholars.
If one attains the essential core of the principles, then one may look back upon all that was previously read.
I write: The realm [of the mind] is vast and open; when the six directions are unobstructed and the four gates are wide open, one achieves the ultimate economy of mental and physical energy.

Nevertheless, a seeker of the Way must possess a sincere and earnest resolve directed toward it. As the ancients said, "If the subordinate is not refined, they shall not attain the truth"—this is no empty word.
It was in this way that Cong was recognized and appreciated by Minister Ming; it is also a fundamental principle for confronting affairs.
Furthermore, Master Heshang, who succeeded Foxing Tai, once offered a verse on the karmic conditions regarding the First Patriarch Jue Tiezi’s statement, “The First Patriarch did not say this”:
“Who says the First Patriarch did not say this? The scorched-tail tiger is originally a tiger. The hornet does not cling to its old nest;
How could a fierce general die at home? Quickly fix your eyes and look back! If you understand how to cut off the stream, where will it go?”
He set out. A pure breeze followed his every step across the land. He also composed a verse on the story of eating dregs of wine:
"Within the thicket of brambles he proclaims the wondrous meaning; amidst the garden of thorns he radiates brilliant light. Of thousands of words and myriad phrases, no one understands;
yet as he follows the warbling oriole over the low wall, the Buddha-nature is revealed. Fojian deeply approved of this. When Foji passed through Hengyang, he sent a verse to him, saying:
Moving among those of different kinds, he was beyond the suspicion of the world; thus he taught that the Buddha-sun might be temporarily obscured by clouds.

Having never heard of his compassionate vow to deliver sentient beings, he instead appeared once more in Nan’an. He stayed at Huītong in Tán, not seeking fame for his time, and therefore his name was not heard in the world.
Master Yuan studied under Yuanwu and attained realization. When Minister Geng Longxue appointed him to reside at Nanyingshan in Chu Prefecture, he remained there for nearly two years.
Becoming weary of the constant welcoming and seeing off of visitors, he addressed the assembly, citing the verse by Gan Tie-mian: "The monastery is a monastery within the Great Song Empire;

The prefecture is a prefecture within the Great Song Empire. Since this monastery within the prefecture cannot accommodate me, What prevents me from traveling with my single bowl across the five lakes?"
Yuan said, "This indeed means going and staying are free and at ease; it reveals one's very wind and bone. I have a verse: Rest! Rest! Rest!
The evening sun goes west as the waters flow east. Only the soaring clouds, their momentum far-reaching, Strike the wind at ninety thousand li and pass beyond the southern provinces.
Having finished, he descended from his seat and departed.

When Yuanwu was serving as the head of the assembly at Wuzu’s monastery, a monk requested instruction on Fengxue’s saying regarding how speech and silence involve transcendence and subtlety, and how one might pass through them without violating the causal conditions.
It happened that Fojian arrived, and Yuanwu said, "Brother Qin, you should compose a verse for him to give to him.
Fojian then composed this verse: "A divine immortal appears amidst the shadows of colored clouds, Holding a red silk fan to veil her face. Hurry!"
"You must look at the immortal; do not look at the hand-fan held by the immortal. Wuzu was deeply awakened and greatly rejoiced.

Later, when the monk looked at Zhenjing’s words and composed this verse regarding the causes and conditions of Mañjuśrī giving rise to views of the Buddha and views of the Dharma, he asked Wuzu about it.
Wuzu said, "As for this verse of his, it is perfectly applicable to all the karmic occasions involving Buddhas and patriarchs."
Zhang Wujin was reading the *Xuedou Niangu* at the Jietan Monastery in Jiangning Prefecture.

Upon reaching the anecdote concerning Baizhang’s visit to Mazu, he remarked, “A fine gold from a great smelting furnace should remain unchanged in color. Suddenly, he threw down the scroll and said, “If the words are truly as such...”
"How could Linji have attained his present status otherwise? There is a verse that says: Linji’s single shout at Daxiong Peak Pierced the skull and left it deaf for three days;
When Huangbo heard it, he was so startled he stuck out his tongue. From this, the House Style was established in Jiangxi.
He once mentioned this to Master Ping, who later sent a letter to Wujin, saying: "Last summer, while reading the lineage of Linji..."
Knowing deeply that the Layman had attained great capacity and great function, [Wumen] sought out the draft of his previous verse. Wumen then sent him another verse, saying:

"The tongue protruded and the ears went deaf—the Master has already understood. Beating one’s breast, one can do nothing but cry out to the blue heavens. In the assembly at Panshan, he performed a somersault;
Only upon reaching this point does one know the madness of Puhua. This was in the third year of the Daguan era.
During the Zhenzong era, Master Deng of Changlu in Zhenzhou renovated Changlu Temple over several years.
Once the work was completed, one night he dreamed of a divine being who came to request that he serve as the temple’s protector deity (tudi). Deng said, "You cannot be my protector deity."
The deity asked, "Why? Deng replied, "You have seen my faults as a monk. The deity said, "I have made a solemn vow," and then severed one of his arms and presented it [to him].
Deng said, "If it is thus, then it may be done," and he subsequently built a shrine for him. When the local tutelary deity (Tudi) was being sculpted, one arm fell off;
though it was repaired many times, it always returned to its former state. Only then did he realize the gravity of the deity's vow.
In the assembly of Chan Master Puzhao, there was an elderly monk who daily recited the *Mahākaruṇā-dhāraṇī* three hundred times;
he did the same for various other sutras and dhāraṇīs. At night, he would invariably perform three hundred prostrations before the Buddha.
Seeing him thus laboring incessantly and without leisure, Xuetang one day said to him, "Why do you not let go of everything? He replied, "As soon as I let go..."
Jue remarked, "You are passing your time idly. Xuetang said, "If you let go, you will not pass your time idly.
He then said to the assembly, "This is all because the power of faith has not yet been fully realized. Therefore, I have always told my brothers: do not get caught up in his 'situations' (ji-jing).
What is meant by 'situations'? The Buddha is called a situation; the Dharma is called a situation; and how much more so are literary compositions and all other things?"
Is it not a matter of miscellaneous affairs? If you maintain a state of leisurely detachment, you will naturally become empty yet spiritual, still yet wondrous—just like a gourd floating on water.
You will drift freely without restraint or fetters; when pressed, you move; when nudged, you turn.
Thus, you truly attain great sovereign freedom.
In Shuzhou there was a lay practitioner who regularly went to the Fifth Patriarch’s monastery to provide meals for the monks. One day he asked the Head Seat, “I am a layman;
can I practice Chan? The Head Seat replied, “Since you are a layman, how could you practice Chan? The layman did not understand.
He presented this to Master Yan, who said, "The Head Seat indeed possesses the authentic means to benefit others. Only then did the layman believe;
he subsequently devoted himself earnestly to investigation. Later, he met Fuyan, who extended his hand and asked, "Why do you call this a hand?"
The layman suddenly attained great enlightenment.

As for Wuzu, while at his monastery of ordination, he was prostrating to each word of the Lotus Sutra. One night, when he came to the character for "excrement" (shǐ) and was about to chant the prostration, he was suddenly struck with doubt.
He then said to the elder monks, "How can even the character for 'excrement' be called a 'Dharma-treasure'? My prostrations have reached this point."
His doubts remained unresolved. An elder monk said, "Based on what you have asked, you should travel south to seek instruction;
you are truly a vessel of the highest caliber for the Gate of the School. The Patriarch then traveled south. Upon first arriving at Xingyuan Prefecture, he stayed there for some time.

While attending to the requests of various monasteries, he slightly deviated from his original resolve. When his former master heard of this, he sent a letter to the Patriarch. When the Patriarch opened the seal, he saw only—
Two lines of verse read: "Since you have managed to escape the vinegar jar, you have instead been submerged in the soy sauce vat.

After reading this, the Patriarch (Zhaozhou) set out for Zhejiang that very day to visit Yuanzhao. Subsequently, he met Fushan Yuan, who, recognizing his extraordinary capacity, directed him to see Baiyun Yuan.
Baiyun showed him the teaching: "The World-Honored One has a secret word; Kāśyapa did not conceal it."
[He was] practicing for a long time without attaining realization. One day, as he hurried up the corridor toward the Dharma Hall, his doubts were suddenly extinguished.

Not long after, he was appointed as the head of the mill. One day, Baiyun went to the mill yard and said, "There have been several monks coming from Mount Lu who can explain Chan, they can deliver lines of verse, and they can even critique the ancients. Baizhang said, "Master..."
"Furthermore, what do you say? Duan replied, "I told him, 'It is truly not yet so. Upon hearing these words, the Patriarch lost his appetite for food and drink for several days;
it was only after seven days that he finally understood their significance. The Patriarch often said to his students, "Because of this, I broke into a cold sweat all over my body;
from then on, I clearly understood the cool breeze of a whole cartload. Xuetang composed a verse on this: [Verse omitted as per instructions]
It is said: A single blow behind the head destroys the total mechanism. Bare and naked, there is nothing to take up; stark and clear, one is free from hooks and needles.
To whom shall this breeze, carried down from the boat, be entrusted?

Zhang Wujin entered the Dongtai (Eastern Terrace) office. While discussing Wen Lugong and Lü Shengong, [the official] did not respond. Zhang requested to leave his post to serve as the Supervisor of Jingnan.

There he met Daohao, who was wearing a coarse cloth loincloth; Hao recommended himself to the Governor of Yingzhou via a letter. As the position at Dayang Monastery happened to be vacant, Zhang subsequently presented him for that role.
While at Lumen in Xiangzhou, Daohao accepted an invitation and said, "For seven years I have eaten the rice of Lumen; now I shall defecate [upon it]."
"Lumen’s dung—do not practice Lumen’s Chan. If you are a sharp-witted monk, then come see me at Dayang.

He then took up his staff and went straight to Yingzhou. He entered the monastery first and only afterwards visited the local administration. The officials rebuked him, saying, "Elder, by what authority did you enter the monastery?
Haoran replied, "I am a man of the mountains and forests; who cares for your provincial and county protocols? Thereupon, he departed.
Holding his staff, Huihao returned to Lumeng. Wujin again sent a letter urging the Governor of Ying, saying:
"Hao is a man of the Way; he cannot be constrained by worldly etiquette. You should extend further courtesy in inviting him. The governor acted according to these words, and Hao arrived at Dayang.
Before long, Wujin sent a letter saying, "I have long thirsted for your instruction; I regret that I am constrained by my official duties and cannot personally attend upon you.
When Hao saw the letter, he remarked, "I am not a dead man! He then took up his staff and traveled to Jingzhu to see Wujin.
Such was his straightforwardness. Later, when Wujin invited him to reside at Yuyuan and ascend the hall, all the officials assembled there.
Hao ascended the hall, looked out at the assembly, and said, "Do you not see? After a long pause, he spoke again, "Do you not see?
Zhang Cao, speaking with a Shu accent, replied, "The Master sees. Hao responded immediately, "It is enough that you, Excellency, see," and then descended from his seat.
One day, as the assembly had gathered, Daohao asked, "What are you doing? They replied, "Entering the room for meditation. Daohao said, "Wait for me to relieve myself first.
When he returned from the latrine, he saw that the monks had not left; he drove them away with his staff. One day, he spoke for the sake of Zhang Wujin.
Master Fu’s verse says: Empty-handed, I grasp a hoe; Walking, I ride a water buffalo. A person passes over the bridge;
The bridge flows, but the water does not flow. Furthermore, he cites Dongshan’s verse: On the summit of Mount Wutai, clouds steam rice;
Before the steps of the Buddha Hall, it is a "dog-urine day. At the top of the bannerpole, *zhuanzi* are being fried; Three monkeys toss coins at night.
These three verses only eulogize matters pertaining to the Dharma-body’s phenomenal aspect; they do not eulogize that which lies beyond the Dharma-body.
Zhang said, "I request the Master to provide a verse. The Master said: "Last night the rain poured down in torrents, Knocking down the grape arbor.

The administrators, attendants, laborers, and men of strength— Those who were to prop it up did so, Those who were to support it did so. Prop and support continued until daybreak; As before, it remains pitiable."
Sheng Hao was a native of Danling in Meizhou. He once fashioned a loincloth (*vṛṣaṇasakthika*) and wrote the names of the successive patriarchs upon it before wearing it.
He remarked, "Only Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra are slightly superior. He further inscribed these names upon his sash;
thus, the community of practitioners referred to him as "Hao the Loincloth-Wearer."
Master Kong was a man of stubborn integrity. Having served Sīxin for a long time, he wished to take his leave. Sīxin said, "Your merit is meager; you should nourish yourself.
Thus, Cāotáng composed a verse to see him off, which says: "For ten years we have gathered at Longfeng Monastery; With one awakening to true emptiness, the myriad realms are at rest.
From now on, follow conditions and remain in lofty seclusion; Do not let your name fall among the common folk. Later...
Dàokōng went to Nántáng in Hángchén. Within a few months, he suffered a fire. He sighed in regret, saying, "I have violated the words of my former teacher; therefore, there is the calamity of today.
A wealthy man alone invited Dàokōng to his residence, intending to build three gates for him. Dàokōng declined, saying, "The gentleman wishes to bestow wealth to seek merit;
this is not a gift for an elder to receive. If you were to instruct me to eat apart from the assembly, it would be improper."
He did not desire it. He practiced his Way with diligence and consequently was not conscripted for labor on earthworks or timber projects.
Chan Master Biaozhao had long studied under Cheng Kumu; however, having a prior grievance with Cheng, he left the monastery to reside at Shenxi in the capital, whereupon he succeeded Touzi Qing.
Upon opening the hall and descending from the seat, Chan Master Shenggang Jiyuan asked: "What have you seen that..."
He succeeded to Touzi. Baoshou said, "I have attained realization by looking at the *yulu* (recorded sayings);
you must not let this down. Jiyin asked, "In what phrase? Baoshou had no words. Jiyin gave him a punch, whereupon Baoshou lost his resolve and the Way declined.

Later, while residing at Fuzhou Puxian Monastery, Old Chan Master Dai composed a preface for the monastery, saying: "If one recognizes the ancients within a phrase, one immediately considers oneself [enlightened]..."

Deceiving the various sages, there is the silent transmission of the intent from the ancient masters of the pagoda. Reviving the fallen tradition of the Blue Avataṃsaka, this family lineage has been passed down for a thousand years;
these two elders stand alone, peerless in their mastery.
The Dharma Master Huizhi traveled to Mount Emei and subsequently entered meditative absorption within a great tree by the roadside in Jiazhou.

In the fourth month of the third year of the Zhenghe era, a violent storm arose and the tree was broken down. A magistrate on patrol passed by and saw that the master’s hair and beard covered his body and his fingernails curled around his limbs;
finding this quite extraordinary, he reported it to the imperial court. An edict was issued ordering [the remains] to be borne [to the capital].
The carriage arrived at the capital. At that time, the Tripitaka Master from West India emerged from his meditative absorption with a golden gong and asked, "In what era does this monk live?
The Dharma Master replied, "I am the younger brother of Dhyānabhadra of Donglin; having traveled to Mount Emei, I have lost track of how much time has passed."
He asked again, "Is Dharma Master Huiyuan still alive? Zongchi replied, "He passed away seven hundred years ago;
how could he still be here? Thereupon, he ceased speaking further. Zongchi asked, "Since you have arrived here, to which direction do you wish to return? The Master said, "To Chenliu County."
He entered meditative absorption once more.
Emperor Huizong commanded an artist to paint his likeness for circulation and bestowed upon him three verses. The first says:
"For seven hundred years, this ancient adept— Who could know the news from within his concentration? How can it compare to departing westward with a single shoe? Birth and death are but weary toil."
"Make a skin. It is also said: "To hide the mountain in the marsh is also to hide the self. In the world, there is no Way to be hidden that can be approached.
Send word to Zhuang Zhou: cease your deliberations. Within these words, there is no one who fails to advance. Again, on the third day: "The sentient body is not insentient;
each and every person is the body within samādhi. If you understand that Bodhi fundamentally has no tree, there is no need for arduous toil."
When asked about Lu Neng, Sishin praised his portrait, saying: "For seven hundred years he has been deceiving the common folk;
with a single thought of transcendence, he roams freely throughout the world."
Yang-shan once sought instruction from Hei-tang. When Hei-tang passed away, Yang-shan oversaw the funeral arrangements and invited the Elder Bing-ju of Sheng Temple to preside over the cremation;
however, the fire would not ignite. Yang-shan looked toward Si-xin and said, "The Master’s intention was nothing other than this:
he wished for this madman to speak a few words. Si-xin replied, "I am currently bound by the observance of mourning rites; I decline."
As he was departing, Shanyu forced him to stay. Sishin held up a torch and said, "This is no mere calamity that would bring trouble upon me;
my transgressions are as vast as the heavens and cannot be pardoned. Now, with both feet trailing through the air, I shall become neither ox nor donkey.
He then struck a circle with the torch and said, "I shall settle this grievance right here," and he cast down the torch, which ignited at his touch.
Incense.
When the Fifth Patriarch, Master Zizhu, resided at Dongshan, there were many seekers of Chan who requested to be enrolled as residents.
Being unable to attend to them all, he posted a notice in the quarters of the attendants which read: "Dongshan has three phrases; if you can speak them, you shall be enrolled. Xuetang.
The Master said, "In my view, this truly opens the door wide. Some went to the attendants' quarters and asked, 'We do not know what those three phrases of the Master are.
The Hall Master said, 'How can I speak with a Chan practitioner such as this?
One day, a brother took his sitting mat and went straight to the Abbot's quarters, saying to himself, 'I cannot express it; it is simply..."
When someone requests to be enrolled as a resident monk, [the abbot] is greatly pleased and calls the *vina* (chant leader) to arrange a place by the bright window.
Yet, if the present-day brothers allow their minds to seek such enrollment, they have already been outside the gate long ago.
Zhangshu Cizhu (Jingchun) received his full ordination at Huadu Monastery in Fuzhou. He had long studied under Master Bao Fengxiang.
Chün composed ten poems on mountain dwelling, the first of which says: "Fearing the cold, I am too lazy to shave my tangled hair; Loving the warmth, I frequently add more firewood to the hearth."
Lilong’s *kāṣāya* was disarrayed and in dishevelment; who could exert such effort to arrange it? Xiang saw this and admonished him, saying:
"This poem is no inferior to that of Guankui. I fear that the world will seek you out for your literary skill rather than believing in your Way."
The Master of Miaokong Hermitage, Miaopu, was a native of Xichuan. He studied under Chan Master Sishin and later established a hermitage at Huating.

There he instructed others according to their capacities, living with a sense of ease and spontaneity. He had a verse for the assembly which says: "Do not dwell upon effort throughout the twelve periods of the day;
Examine, examine until you reach the infinite. You must penetrate thoroughly to the bottom of that infinity, And trample the Mount Sumeru to pieces."
At the First Peak, one day, wishing to set sail upon the sea, he took leave of the monastics and laypeople and spoke this verse:

"To sit and depart, or to stand and pass away, is not as good as a water burial. First, it saves wood for cremation; second, it avoids digging a grave. To let go of the hand and simply go—how unimpeded and refreshing!
Who is the one who knows this? It is the Boatman Monk. His lofty style is difficult to follow for a thousand or ten thousand years. A single song of the fisherman."

Few people raised the chant. Thereupon, he ascended a lacquered basin, unfurled a cloth sail, and with hands raised in gratitude to the fourfold assembly, blew his iron flute into the midst of the surging waves and submerged himself.
Three days later, when the tide receded, he was found sitting in the full-lotus posture upon a sandbank, his countenance and spirit unmoved.
Several tens of thousands of fellow practitioners welcomed him back to Qinglong Monastery, where they made offerings for five days. [At the end of the tea ceremony...]
The *vibhīṣaṇa* relics were five-colored like pearls and beyond counting. A pair of cranes circled overhead for an entire day before the fire was extinguished and they departed.
His stupa was enshrined at Qinglong; his lifespan was seventy-one years.
Jiaoshan Cheng Kumu and Zhao Chanti both succeeded Furong Daokai; they received the Dharma at different times and never knew one another.
While Zhao resided at Baofeng, his reputation for the Way was widespread, yet Cheng remained unaware of his standing. Consequently, neither of them corresponded with the other’s disciples.
Zhao therefore dispatched his attendant Peng to beg alms throughout Jiang and Zhejiang. Zhao himself inscribed his own portrait, saying: "Rain."
The pale pink peach calyx is fresh and washed clean; the wind shakes the light green willow filaments so gently. Within the shadows of white clouds, strange rocks are revealed;
amidst the luster of emerald waters, ancient trees are serene. *Ei!* Who are you? Chengjian sighed and said, "Only today do I know that this person has personally met the former master.
Longpeng then requested the praise. Cheng said, "Have you not seen Fayan?"
He took up the story of Jia Shan’s “state” (jing) and said, "For twenty years I understood it only as a state. At this, Peng suddenly attained realization.
*Xuetang Xing Heshang Shiyilu* (The Record of the Collected Omissions of Master Xuetang Xing), end.
